title: Henry Sugar
logline: A bored, wealthy gambler reads a nested account of a man who taught himself to see — and spends years in the boring work of learning, until the card turns over and the world is much larger than advertised.
blueprint: Dahl Henry Sugar engine — faithful structural retelling for adults; Real Magic with a k (Radin thesis, Dahl fable); Dispenza / Radin / Sheldrake as in-world gospel
market: literary wonder / consciousness-curious readers (Dahl · Dispenza · Radin · Sheldrake) — the card-turn moment, played straight
lineage: Roald Dahl, The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar (1977) — structural fidelity, original prose
